CVE-2026-104813.title: Improper limitation of a pathname to a restricted directory ('pat ...
CVE-2026-104813.description:
Improper limitation of a pathname to a restricted directory ('path traversal') vulnerability in Apache BuildStream allows malicious or compromised artifact or execution servers to write files on the host, with the privileges of the user running BuildStream, as part of `bst artifact checkout`.

The impact of this issue is mitigated by:

  *  BuildStream projects should only use trusted servers for remote cache and remote execution as otherwise the build output can also not be trusted


This issue affects Apache BuildStream: through 2.8.1.
Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.8.2, which fixes the issue.

CVE-2026-111600.title: UNIX symbolic link (symlink) following vulnerability in Apache Bu ...
CVE-2026-111600.description:
UNIX symbolic link (symlink) following vulnerability in Apache BuildStream allows source plugins to inadvertently read or write files on the host, with the privileges of the user running BuildStream, via symlinks from malicious or compromised source archives or respositories, as part of source fetching.

The impact of this issue is mitigated by:

  *  BuildStream projects should only use trusted sources in their elements as otherwise the build output can also not be trusted
  *  None of the source plugins in the buildstream, buildstream-plugins or buildstream-plugins-community repositories use the vulnerable `open_file` method


This issue affects Apache BuildStream: through 2.8.1.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.8.2, which fixes the issue.

CVE-2026-82331.title: Improper link resolution before file access ('link following') vu ...
CVE-2026-82331.description:
Improper link resolution before file access ('link following') vulnerability in the `tar` source plugin of Apache BuildStream running on Python < 3.12 allows malicious source tarballs to write files on the host, with the privileges of the user running BuildStream, via symlinks as part of source fetching.
The impact of this issue is mitigated by:

* BuildStream projects should only use trusted sources in their elements as otherwise the build output can also not be trusted
* Tracking a source tarball pins its SHA256 hash, which prevents MITM attacks of users that are fetching an already tracked project
* When running on Python >= 3.12, BuildStream >= 2.3.0 already makes use of the Python `tarfile` filter functionality, which blocks the symlink escape

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.8.1, which fixes this issue.
